topStories.headline: Compass Datacenters Gives Red Oak ISD $5 Million to Plug a Sudden Cash-Flow Gap
topStories.dek: The data-center company's one-time gift is meant to offset an unexpected shift in state funding and the district's entry into recapture.
topStories.body:
Red Oak Independent School District announced this week that Compass Datacenters has donated $5 million to the district — a one-time gift aimed at cushioning a financial shortfall caused by two simultaneous pressures: a change in the state's funding payment schedule and the district's transition into recapture status. Together, those two factors created an estimated $15 million to $20 million cash-flow gap, much of it tied directly to payroll.

The district will have roughly $2.5 million withheld by the state this year under the recapture formula. District officials said they are also reviewing spending and making adjustments to protect classroom instruction and essential operations as they absorb the longer-term effects of the new fiscal reality.

Because both recapture and the revised payment schedule are expected to continue, Red Oak ISD intends to set aside a portion of the donation to help manage future cash-flow needs and potential borrowing costs — rather than spending it all at once.

Compass is one of Red Oak's largest property-tax payers, having paid more than $5.1 million in school property taxes to the district in 2025. The company stressed that this charitable donation is entirely separate from those required tax payments. The gift builds on an already substantial local investment by Compass, which has previously funded a $15 million Ellis County animal shelter and a $12.6 million workforce-training facility tied to Texas State Technical College in Red Oak.

topStories.headline: Midlothian Voters Head to the Polls Tuesday on a $192.45 Million Bond Package
topStories.dek: Five propositions on the November 3 ballot would fund roads, a police substation, drainage, and new parks for a city now topping 47,000 residents.
topStories.body:
Early voting closes today, October 30, and Election Day arrives Tuesday, November 3, as Midlothian residents decide the fate of a $192.45 million bond package that city leaders say is needed to keep pace with rapid population growth. The city's population now exceeds 47,000, according to the city's own news release.

The package is divided into five separate propositions. Proposition A is the largest at $102.3 million, directed entirely at street projects. Proposition B would fund a new police substation at $6.81 million. Proposition C sets aside $10 million for drainage studies and improvements. Proposition D allocates $47.26 million for existing park projects, while Proposition E provides $26.09 million for two brand-new parks.

The bond package was shaped by a citizens planning committee that reviewed the city's finances, road conditions, and infrastructure before recommending the five-proposition structure to the council. If approved in full, the funding would be drawn down over five years. Voters can find polling and early-voting information at midlothianbond.com.

topStories.headline: Midlothian Police Chief Carl Smith Installed as President of North Texas Police Chiefs Association
topStories.dek: Smith, who has led the Midlothian Police Department since 2007, was formally installed in the association's top leadership post last week.
topStories.body:
Midlothian Police Chief Carl Smith was installed last week as President of the North Texas Police Chiefs Association (NTPCA), according to a report published Wednesday by the Ellis County Press. Smith has served as Midlothian's police chief since he was hired on July 16, 2007, coming to the city after a 20-year career in DeSoto where he rose to the rank of assistant chief.

The NTPCA supports the Texas Police Chiefs Association in promoting professional development for law enforcement executives and managers across the state, and facilitates networking among police leaders throughout North Texas. The presidency follows a structured ladder of offices — treasurer, secretary, second vice president, first vice president — before an officer serves a one-year term as president.

Smith holds a Master of Science in Criminal Justice Management from Sam Houston State University and has completed training at the FBI National Academy in Quantico, Virginia. He also serves as an adjunct professor at the Tarleton State University campus in Midlothian.

moreNews.headline: New Apartment Community Opens in Red Oak with Public Fishing Pond
moreNews.body: Greystar, in partnership with Whitman Peterson, opened Halden at Red Oak on October 20 — a new rental community just off Highway 342, about 20 miles south of downtown Dallas. At the city's request, Greystar preserved and upgraded an existing on-site pond for public use, adding piers and a paved trail that loops around the water. The community offers one- and two-bedroom apartments as well as three- and four-bedroom single-family homes for rent, with amenities including a fitness center, pool, outdoor terrace with fire pit, and an outdoor kitchen. Two future retail spaces are also planned on the site.
